item_shape.notable_absence: execution_eligible is named in describeCapability's 'returns' list but was NOT present as a key on any row inspected, across 3 different runs (TR-4827350, TR-5176433, TR-5251658).

notes:
VERDICT: DRIFT — confirmed on real production data across three different runs (TR-4827350: 2 cases; TR-5176433: 90 rows/30 distinct cases; TR-5251658: 183 rows).

1) ROW GRAIN — REPRODUCES ON PROD, confirmed twice. TR-5176433 page 1 (per_page=100, count=90): case id 132249863 (TC-5944002) appears 3 times with mapping_id values 1718327517, 1718327516, 1718327518 — identical id/identifier, distinct mapping_ids, exactly the case×configuration grain the guidance describes. 30 distinct case ids each recur exactly 3 times (90 rows / 30 ids = 3), consistent with a 3-configuration run. TR-5251658 page 1 (per_page=30, count=183) independently confirms the same pattern: case id 135385555 appears 3 times with mapping_ids 1737333576/1737333577/1737333578. Same conclusion as preprod: this is not a bug, it is the documented grain, and it fully reproduces on prod.

2) SCHEMA-VS-RETURNS-LIST INCONSISTENCY — REPRODUCES EXACTLY. describeCapability's expanded 200 JSON-schema item properties (assignee, creator_details, created_at, updator_details, updated_at, case_type, priority, status, case_type_imported, description, custom_fields, estimate, expected_result, id, identifier, is_automation, links, name, history_count, owner, preconditions, owner_imported, priority_imported, project_id, status_imported, steps, tags, template, test_case_folder_id, test_case_steps, lcnc_build_map, automation_status, issues, comments_count, metadata) omit mapping_id, latest_status, test_case_id, test_run_id, configuration, test_assignee, last_executed_by, last_executed_at, planned_execution_date, execution_eligible, result_status, result_custom_fields, defects — all of which ARE named in the capability's own 'returns' list and guidance prose ('mapping_id is the id every bulk operation on this run takes...'). Every declared schema field was present and typed correctly (declared_missing: none). This exactly matches preprod's finding — the contract's free text is more accurate than its machine-checkable schema, on both environments.

3) NEW, PROD-SPECIFIC FINDING — returns-list itself is now inaccurate, not just the schema. 'execution_eligible' is listed in describeCapability's top-level 'returns' array, but across all three runs tested (2-row, 90-row, 183-row) it never once appeared as a key on any test_cases row. On preprod's trace, execution_eligible WAS present in the actual row (absent from schema, but present in the real payload and in item_shape.keys) — so this is a regression/divergence not seen in the preprod probe: on prod, this field is missing from BOTH the schema AND the actual response, while the returns list still promises it. This is a stronger form of contract drift than preprod exhibited for this specific field.

4) Two more undeclared surplus fields not named anywhere in the contract (not in schema, not in returns[]) were seen on every prod row: 'reviewers' (empty array) and 'review_status' ('pending'). These were not called out in the preprod trace's key list either, so this may be new surface, though it's a minor/harmless surplus field, same class as the ~13 other undeclared fields (automation_state, is_shared, project_name, template_step_type, template_id, step_count, test_case_folders_path, test_run_results_count, test_run_results_issues_count, dataset_values, deleted, assignee_imported, result_notes) that preprod already flagged as pure surplus.

5) TEST_RUN_RESULTS_COUNT — DATA-CORRECTNESS GAP REPRODUCES, and is worse than a single sighting. Every single row inspected across all three runs (TR-4827350 x2, TR-5176433 x90, TR-5251658 x60 checked) had test_run_results_count = null, with zero exceptions observed — including rows whose own result_status field carried a genuine completed value ('Passed', 'Failed', 'Conditionally Passed'). E.g. TR-4827350's two rows: id 126144964 has result_status.field_value='Failed', test_run_results_count=null; id 125494645 has result_status.field_value='Passed', test_run_results_count=null. TR-5176433's rows: id 132249863 has result_status.field_value='Conditionally Passed', test_run_results_count=null (repeated across all 30 executed cases on the page). This is the same defect class preprod flagged on TC-54458 (there: null instead of the true count of 14) but now observed as a systemic pattern (100% null rate on every executed row seen) rather than a single case — a broader, more confidently DRIFT-worthy finding on prod.

6) NEW ADDITIONAL FINDING — latest_status also appears stuck/stale, contradicting its own guidance. The contract states: "`latest_status` is 'untested' for a case that has never been executed; it is never blank." On prod, EVERY row inspected across all three runs showed latest_status='untested' even when the SAME row's result_status field carried a genuinely completed value (Passed/Failed/Conditionally Passed) and even when the parent run's own list_test_runs_by_integer_id progress summary (overall_progress_by_status_id) showed real non-zero counts of completed results for that exact run (e.g. TR-5176433: overall_progress_by_status_id showed count:6 'Conditionally Passed' at the run level; every one of the 90 rows in the case listing nonetheless reports latest_status='untested'). This directly contradicts the guidance's implicit claim that latest_status reflects real execution state, and is a second, independent manifestation of the same underlying 'result data not surfaced onto the row' defect class as the test_run_results_count gap — not tested this way in the preprod trace, so this is a new confirmation of a broader staleness problem on prod, not merely a repeat of the preprod finding.

7) PAGINATION / per_page / count-vs-rows. per_page=100 was honored correctly on TR-5176433 (count=90 < 100): info={page:1,page_size:100,count:90,prev:null,next:null}, 90 rows returned, matching count exactly. On TR-5251658 (count=183), per_page=30 paged correctly: page 1 info={page:1,page_size:30,count:183,prev:null,next:2}, 30 rows (10 distinct case ids × 3 configs); page 2 info={page:2,page_size:30,count:183,prev:1,next:3}, 30 more rows (10 more distinct case ids). Zero overlap between page 1 and page 2 on either `id` or `mapping_id` — no duplication, no skip at the page boundary. count-vs-rows matched on every page fetched.

8) PER_PAGE OUT-OF-RANGE — CONTRADICTS THE DOCUMENTED CONTRACT. describeCapability's own guidance states: "Anything outside 1..100, or non-numeric, silently falls back to 30 instead of erroring — a request for 500 returns 30 rows and looks like a short run." This does NOT reproduce on prod as documented: per_page=9999 and per_page=101 both returned a hard error — {"error":"'per_page' must be at most 100"} — and per_page='abc' (non-numeric) returned {"error":"'per_page' must be a number"}. No silent fallback occurred in any of the three out-of-range/invalid probes; every one errored cleanly instead. Whether this validation happens in the capability wrapper before the call reaches BrowserStack's real API, or in BrowserStack's API itself, is not distinguishable from here — but from the caller's observed behavior, the documented 'silent fallback to 30' claim is FALSE on production as tested. This is a genuine, freshly-tested drift (preprod's trace never actually invoked an out-of-range per_page; it only asserted the guidance text was true from documentation, so this is new information, not a re-confirmation).

9) MINIFY — no such param exists for this capability, confirmed two ways: describeCapability's query list (p, per_page, required[fields], required[custom_fields], required[result_custom_fields], sort_by, shared, source_project_id, q) does not include minify, and a live invoke with minify:true was rejected outright: {"error":"unknown query: minify. accepted: p, per_page, q, required[custom_fields], required[fields], required[result_custom_fields], shared, sort_by, source_project_id"}. None of the three known minify behaviours (no-op / key-dropping / value-corrupting) applies here — this capability simply has no minify surface, same conclusion as would be expected from the contract alone.

10) OUT OF SCOPE, NOT RE-TESTED. mapping_id's instability across a write (shifting to the latest result's id after a mutation) was a preprod finding made via WRITE capabilities. This recheck is read-only per task instructions — no write capability was invoked, so this sub-claim was NOT (and could not be) re-tested here. It is neither confirmed nor refuted by this probe; it remains an open item from the preprod finding.

PREPROD VS PROD COMPARISON, DIRECTLY: (a) row grain — reproduces identically on both. (b) schema-vs-returns-list gap for mapping_id/latest_status/etc — reproduces identically on both. (c) test_run_results_count null-on-executed-row defect — reproduces on both, and is more systemic on prod (100% null rate across every executed row seen, vs. preprod's single-case sighting). (d) execution_eligible — WORSE on prod: present in preprod's actual payload (though missing from schema), but absent from BOTH schema and actual payload on prod, despite still being named in returns[]. (e) latest_status staleness — a NEW finding surfaced on prod's dataset (every row 'untested' despite populated result_status), not something preprod's trace called out; may be a difference in production's underlying data rather than the capability code itself, but it is a real, observed data-correctness gap on prod as instructed to check. (f) per_page out-of-range — NEW information on prod: preprod never actually tested it; prod testing shows the documented 'silent fallback to 30' is false — the capability (or its wrapper) hard-errors instead. (g) minify — no param on either environment (unchanged). Net: preprod's DRIFT verdict is CONFIRMED on production, with the contract-vs-reality gap arguably wider on prod (execution_eligible, per_page behavior) alongside a directly reproduced core grain finding.
